introduction: Idaho CareLine is the state’s free community-resource referral service. Specialists answer Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m. Mountain Time; you can call or text for help locating services.

sections.who: You do not need a public-benefit approval to ask for a referral. Eligibility for an actual service is determined by its provider.
sections.get: CareLine connects people with food, housing, healthcare and other community resources. It is operated by Idaho’s Department of Health and Welfare.

sections.apply:
1. Contact a specialist

    Dial 211 or 800-926-2588, or text 898211 during the published specialist hours.

  2. Explain your need

    Describe your location, immediate problem and providers already contacted.

  3. Follow the referral

    Ask the receiving provider about eligibility, available appointments and documents.
sections.after: If a referral is unsuitable, ask for alternatives. Use the state CareLine page for current contact and online-search options.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Idaho CareLine service and hours. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: No. It provides information and referrals.
The Idaho Department of Health and Welfare operates CareLine.
Is telephone help available all night?
The state publishes weekday specialist hours of 8 a.m.–6 p.m. Mountain Time.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
